sa-rattus-norvegicus.title: Fancy Rat
sa-rattus-norvegicus.summary: Social and interactive, pet rats are bigger and easier to handle than most small rodents, and many enjoy attention. They need at least one rat companion, a big tall cage to climb in and an hour or more out of the cage every day.
rows: A tall wire cage with a solid floor: at least 90 × 60 × 120 cm (about 36 × 24 × 48 in) for 2–5 rats, or 2.5 cubic feet per rat. Not a glass tank. Add hammocks, nest boxes and a litter box; paper bedding (no pine or cedar)

Rat pellets or blocks as the base; small amounts of vegetables, fruit, cooked egg and grains within the daily ration. Avoid onion, citrus, grapes and raisins, rhubarb, walnuts, chocolate, and sugary or fatty foods. Feed morning and evening
Must live in same-sex pairs or groups (or with a neutered male); single rats can become depressed
Generally easier to handle than smaller rodents and many enjoy attention; may nip if frightened. Wash hands after handling
Most active at night and at dawn and dusk; needs at least an hour of playtime outside the cage daily
warn: Noisy or rapid breathing can mean a contagious respiratory infection; see a vet.
